subject: ggplo2 0.9: labeling error when manually dodging discrete scales

messages.author: 746a110d20a6f112
messages.subject: ggplo2 0.9: labeling error when manually dodging discrete scales
parts:
Hi Group-

I have a continuous y axis, a discrete x-axis, and two discrete
'group' in my data. I want to the plot the groups in the same facet,
and I want to dodge each group a little to the left or right, since
the y values from the two groups are very close together. This worked
just fine in the previous version of ggplot2. However after the 0.9
upgrade whenever I manually dodge the x values, the labels on the x
axis convert to numbers instead of the factor labels.

Here is an example of when it worked in the previous version:
http://dl.dropbox.com/u/9577903/Levels_MarEffectsofInteractions_Loss_reglagz.pdf

Here is example of when it does not work in the current version (note
the x-axis labels have changed):
http://dl.dropbox.com/u/9577903/Levels_MarEffectsofInteractions_Loss_reglagz_stateZs.pdf


I have also tried manually labeling the x axis, but that produces
other unexplainable errors. Below is some sample code for reproducing
the errors and some solutions I've tried.

Any advice on how to get the effect I want without losing the x-axis
labels ( as seen in the first linked pdf above) is appreciated.

Thanks

Here is the example:

library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

#----Create The Data
y<-rep(1:5,2)
y<-y+runif(10,-1,1)
d<-data.frame('yax'=y,'xax'=letters[1:5],mod=c('mod1','mod2'))

#--Create the First Plot
pd<-d
jit<-ifelse(pd$mod=='mod1',as.numeric(pd$xax)-.1,as.numeric(pd$xax)+.
1) #Dodge the points in an ordered way
p1<-ggplot(data=pd,aes(x=xax,y=yax,colour=mod,linetype=mod))
p1<-p1+geom_point(aes(x=jit,y=yax))
p1 #X-Axis does not have proper
labels

p2<-p1+scale_x_discrete(name='',labels=levels(pd$xax)) #Produces 'NA's
in the labels
p2

p3<-p1+scale_x_discrete(name='',labels=rep(levels(pd$xax),each=2))
#Shifts the labels to the left
p3

I've got three approaches: label the (now) continuous scale with
discrete values, force the scale to be discrete, or let ggplot do the
dodging for you. They are ordered in increasing goodness of approach (in
my opinion).

Labeling the continuous scale:

p1 + scale_x_continuous(name='', breaks=as.numeric(d$xax),
labels=d$xax[d$xax])

Forcing the discrete scale:

ggplot(data = pd, aes(x = xax, y = yax, colour=mod, linetype=mod)) +
geom_blank() +
geom_point(aes(x = jit))

Note that it would be better if instead of just assigning to jit in the
global space, you made that a column in pd.

Let ggplot do the dodging:

ggplot(data = pd, aes(x = xax, y = yax, colour=mod, linetype=mod)) +
geom_point(position=position_dodge(width=0.4))

This doesn't use your jit variable at all.
